correctness.rationale: Positive definiteness of the truncated moment Gram matrix for support>N and strict eigenvalue boundaries verified by zero counting. Markov–Lukács interval factorization derived from real Fejér–Riesz, with full Cayley change-of-variable and exact degree control, gives |P|^2 + (c-cosθ)/(1-c)|Q|^2. A Rayleigh quotient argument proves the lower bound and completely characterizes equality. Support≤N is handled separately by a vanishing nonnegative trigonometric polynomial. The asymmetric degree-two determinant and symmetrization inequality were derived algebraically; the packaged CHECK.py passed 66 numerical diagnostics, not relied upon for infinite proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating sharp theorem is restricted to symmetric measures. The new formula removes the assumption for every finite positive circle measure, gives sharp computable constants and all equality fibers using N×N Hermitian moment matrices, and separates finite-support degeneration. For any nonzero off-center atom fraction, its exact sharp radius differs strictly from the radius after reflection symmetrization, so the new domain is not cosmetic. This is a motivated structural classification, not just a numeric example or routine arbitrary slice.
